bull_bear.body: Prioritizing hospital capex and bolt-on acquisitions (e.g., Jalandhar); comfortable with 0.96x net debt/EBITDA; open to increasing Agilus stake to 100% if opportunity arises; no dividend or buyback mentioned; cash flow reinvested into growth and digital infrastructure
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: CGHS/ECHS payment delays (180-day receivables); regulatory ambiguity in CGHS rate revisions; integration risks from Gleneagles and Jalandhar; FMRI commissioning delay to Mar'26; dependency on high ARPOB growth without price hikes
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and bullish; emphasized sustained growth momentum, margin expansion beyond guidance, and disciplined M&A; highlighted operational efficiency, digital transformation, and network consolidation as key levers; no caution on macro or demand
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Exit from low-margin Aam Aadmi Mohalla Clinics (Q1FY26) boosted diagnostics margin by 460bps without price hikes; 77% of hospital revenue now comes from 13 high-margin (>20% EBITDA) facilities, indicating successful portfolio optimization; digital revenues (29.5%) now rival physical channel contribution
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Leverage is modest and disclosed on a net basis: Net Debt / (Cash) of INR 2,233 Cr as on 30th June 2026 (Mar 31, 2026: 2,334; Jun 30, 2025: 1,869), with 'Net Debt to EBITDA was at 1.01x vs 0.92x for Q1FY27 and Q1FY26 (basis annualized EBITDA of Q1FY27 and Q1FY26, respectively)'.
- Net Debt to Equity stood at 0.21x at Jun 30, 2026 versus 0.23x at Mar 31, 2026 and 0.20x at Jun 30, 2025, against Shareholder's Equity of INR 10,472 Cr.
- The deck flags that 'Net Debt excludes lease liabilities', which were INR 616 Cr at Jun 30, 2026 versus INR 274 Cr at Jun 30, 2025 — a sharp rise alongside the Greater Noida lease conversion.
- Cash and Cash Equivalents fell to INR 347 Cr at Jun 30, 2026 from INR 538 Cr at Mar 31, 2026, while gross Debt reduced to INR 2,580 Cr from INR 2,872 Cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Cluster-led model across NCR, Punjab, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Mumbai deepening market leadership and clinical collaboration
- Focus specialties (oncology, gastroenterology, neurosciences, renal sciences, orthopaedics, cardiac sciences) grew 19% YoY and contributed 62% of hospital revenues in FY26, similar to FY25
- Integrated hospital + diagnostics platform -- Agilus network of 400+ labs and 4,400+ customer touch points across 1,000+ cities enabling comprehensive/seamless patient care
- Asset-light network expansion via management and lease arrangements -- Gleneagles O&M partnership adds management of ~700 beds across five hospitals without ownership capex
- Investment in robotic-assisted surgery (19 systems network-wide) and AI-enabled diagnostic/medical equipment supporting clinical differentiation and pioneering procedures
- Trusted brand and scale as one of India's largest private hospital networks, with clinical talent and one of the lowest attrition levels cited in the industry
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Legacy regulatory and legal exposure from the erstwhile-promoter era — SEBI issued Show Cause Notices alleging fund diversion of approximately Rs 397.12 crore by the erstwhile promoters (Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh) via subsidiary EHIRCL; SEBI has already imposed penalties (Rs 1 crore on the Company, Rs 1 crore on EHIRCL, Rs 50 lakh on FHsL) and directed monitored recovery of the diverted amount, while the Economic Offences Wing, Enforcement Directorate and SFIO investigations into the Company/its subsidiaries remain ongoing -- a continuing legal/regulatory overhang unrelated to current operations.
- Broad operational, regulatory, HR and financial risk exposure inherent to a competitive healthcare business — Management's MD&A explicitly states the Company is exposed to a broad range of operational, regulatory, human-resources and financial risks characteristic of the healthcare industry, and that while risks cannot be entirely eliminated, only mitigation measures are in place.
- Persistent shortage of skilled clinical talent — The Company operates in a highly competitive healthcare talent market marked by persistent shortages of skilled clinical resources; sustaining low attrition and staffing new/expanding facilities depends on continued success of retention and talent-pipeline initiatives.
- Execution risk on growth strategy, expansion plans and acquisition integration — The Company's forward-looking statement flags its ability to successfully implement strategy, future business plans, growth and expansion, and the impact of any acquisitions as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Uncertain demand growth and general market risk exposure — Management explicitly flags 'the actual growth in demand for our products and services' and 'exposure to market risks' among the factors that could cause results to diverge from forward-looking statements.
- Rising leverage to fund inorganic growth — Net debt rose to INR 2,334 Crores as on March 31, 2026 from INR 1,694 Crores a year earlier (net debt to EBITDA of 1.09x vs 0.93x), an increase management attributes primarily to funding the People Tree Hospital and Shrimann Hospital acquisitions and other investments -- continued acquisitive growth could further build leverage.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body: Further acquisitions in Punjab, NCR, and South India; potential consolidation of Gleneagles O&M assets; expansion of medical travel to 10%+ of revenue; scaling Agilus diagnostics network to 5,000+ touchpoints by FY27
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Digital transformation across hospitals and diagnostics -- expanded EMR deployment (OPD/IPD units), myFortis 3.0 unified patient/agent platform, AI-enabled search and WhatsApp bot, next-gen PACS rollout -- to strengthen clinical workflows and patient experience
- Network expansion through capacity additions, speciality scale-ups and integration of new facilities, pursued via brownfield expansion, acquisitions, lease arrangements and asset-light operating/management partnerships (e.g. Gleneagles O&M)
- Inorganic growth strategy -- acquiring hospital operations (Shrimann Superspecialty Hospital, TMI Healthcare) and entering a greenfield collaboration for a new hospital, to add capacity beyond organic build-out
- People strategy centred on building a future-ready leadership pipeline (Future Operational Leadership Programme with TISS), scaling the Apprentice Programme as a frontline talent pipeline, and sustaining low attrition amid a competitive clinical talent market
- Strengthening information security and resilience (Data Loss Prevention, AI-enabled EDR/XDR, hospital network hardening) as digital adoption increases
- Consolidating brand ownership -- secured Court-confirmed sale of the 'Fortis' brand and allied trademarks in the Company's favour, with registration actions underway
- The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 1 per equity share for FY 2025-26, to be placed for shareholder declaration at the AGM (August 11, 2026). Independent Directors' commission is being placed for shareholder approval for a further three-year period (FY2027-FY2030), indicating continuity of the existing remuneration/governance framework rather than a change in policy.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Fortis is executing a multi-year bed-capacity build-out: management aims to grow its national footprint from ~6,100 beds (including JV and O&M facilities) to more than 7,900 beds over the next four years, driven mainly by brownfield expansion, with a stated plan to add around 1,800 beds through brownfield expansion by FY2029-30. Major named expansion projects are currently underway at FMRI, Shalimar Bagh, Amritsar and Mohali, with phased completion expected over the next few years. During FY2025-26 the network was grown through a mix of brownfield additions (~250 beds, primarily in Manesar, Noida and Faridabad) and inorganic moves: the acquisition of the 125-bedded People Tree Hospital in Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru (with an adjacent land parcel enabling expansion to over 300 beds; consummated January 2026), a 15-year lease of a ~200-bedded multi-specialty hospital in Greater Noida from RR Lifesciences (expandable to ~250 beds; entered September 2025, previously O&M-managed by Fortis), the acquisition of the 228-bedded Shrimann Superspecialty Hospital in Jalandhar with an adjacent land parcel (consummated July 2025), the launch of Adayu, a 36-bedded specialised mental healthcare facility in Gurugram (November 2025), an O&M services agreement with Gleneagles Healthcare India Private Limited to manage ~700 beds across five hospitals and a clinic (entered July 2025), and a collaboration agreement (August 2025) for the operations and management of a 550-bedded greenfield super-specialty hospital to be developed in Lucknow by the Ekana Group. Separately, the Company expanded its robotic-surgery fleet by four systems during the year, taking the network-wide total to 19 robots, and commissioned other high-end medical equipment (soft-tissue surgical robots, MRI machines, Cath labs, a PET-CT).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising healthcare demand driven by population growth (toward 1.5bn by 2030), a growing middle class, ageing demographics and increasing prevalence of lifestyle/non-communicable diseases
- Government-led investment and policy support -- higher Union Budget 2026-27 allocation to health (~10% YoY), PM-ABHIM and PMSSY infrastructure schemes -- expanding healthcare infrastructure and access
- Rising health insurance penetration (35% in FY19 to 41% in FY24) shifting the payment mix from out-of-pocket to insurance-driven, supporting demand for elective procedures
- Growing medical tourism / medical value travel, with the market expected to expand from US$7.69bn (CY24) to US$14.31bn (CY29), supporting the Company's international patient volumes
- Structural undersupply of hospital beds and clinical workforce in India relative to global benchmarks (16 vs 33 beds per 10,000 population; ~10 physicians vs global median ~17 per 10,000), indicating continued headroom for organised private capacity expansion
- Industry-wide capacity build-out -- private hospitals expected to add 4,000+ beds in FY26 -- reflecting broad sectoral growth momentum
- India's healthcare delivery market (hospitals + clinics) projected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR over FY25-30, with the inpatient segment expected to remain over 70% of value
- 550-bed greenfield super-specialty hospital in Lucknow under a collaboration agreement with the Ekana Group -- in development, not yet operational
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Fortis delivered strong Q2FY26 growth with 19.3% hospital revenue growth and 22.9% EBITDA margin, driven by higher ARPOB from oncology and robotic surgeries, while diagnostics margins surged to 26.1% on mix shift; the company is scaling capacity with 550 new beds in H1 and accelerating margin expansion through operational efficiency and network integration.

open.item: Medium-term hospital revenue growth ~14% YoY with ARPOB ~5%-6% and balance from volume/bed expansion.
Legal fees (previously ~INR 30-40 cr/year) expected to reduce ~50% after open offer closure but not to zero (HC case + ex-promoter recovery proceedings continue).
Agilus expected to reach industry-level growth (~8%-10%, largely volume) by Q2/Q3 of FY26.
The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 1 per share for FY 2025-26.
The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 1 per equity share (10% of face value) for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval, with record date July 24, 2026.
FY26 margin guidance (moving 20.5% to 22.5%) likely to be beaten; management expects higher margin improvement than originally guided.
H2 FY26 revenue growth expected similar to H1 (~18%-19%), with Q3 a slight seasonal dip and Q4 stronger.
Hospital ARPOB growth expected ~5%-6% in H2 FY26 (price increase only ~1%-1.5%), rest from mix/robotics/day care.
Overall occupancy (currently ~70%-71%) expected to remain above 70% but below 75% as new capacity comes in H2.
Maintain full-year FY26 organic bed addition of ~400-500 beds (~550 operational beds already added in H1 incl. Jalandhar & Greater Noida).
FMRI 225-bed expansion delayed ~3 months, now expected to commission by March-end (spilling into FY27).
Agilus full-year FY26 EBITDA margin guidance ~23%-24% (H1 at ~24%).
Noida O&M/lease unit expected to reach ~15% EBITDA in ~6 months with medical-equipment and clinical investment.
EMR inpatient module rollout to complete across the network by end of FY26 (4 hospitals live so far).
Adding 4 more robots this year (~INR 12 cr per da Vinci, ~INR 5 cr per ortho robot) to the ~15 already in network.
Gleneagles O&M fee (~3% of ~INR 700 cr revenue) expected to add ~0.2%-0.3% to EBITDA margin, over and above prior FY26 guidance.
Maintain guidance of ~2% (200 bps) margin improvement for FY26 (hospital margins ~22%).
Agilus full-year FY26 EBITDA margin guidance ~22%-23% (net revenue basis).
Hospital revenue expected to grow ~14%-15% in FY26, with ARPOB ~5%-6% and rest from volume.
Expect ~2% (150-200 bps) hospital EBITDA margin expansion in FY26, similar to FY25.
